transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 PST | Duration ~42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lara (Solstice Infra), Samir (CTO), Nina (Security)
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, should be about 40 minutes, we want to walk through our data handling and retention controls, logging redaction, and the request storage toggles in the Console.
[00:12] Lara: yep thanks, we had a quick agenda in the invite, primarily around how we can keep PHI/PII out of logs and meet our 7-year retention for transaction metadata.
[00:22] Ethan: cool, i'll share my screen and open the Redwood Console — sorry audio might be a bit laggy, let me know.
[00:30] Ethan: (screen) okay, starting at the Console home, route settings -> data handling. The main controls are: request storage toggle, automatic PII redaction, custom redaction rules, per-route TTLs and encryption at rest using customer KMS.
[00:47] Samir: quick Q — if we turn off request storage, do we still store metrics/aggregates for usage billing?
[00:53] Ethan: short answer: yes, metrics and token-level billing counters are retained for billing and quota; you can choose to redact or disable storing full request payloads. We emit aggregated usage that's non-reversible for billing.
[01:10] Nina: and audit logs — we need those for SOC2, so even if we redact requests, can we keep the audit trail of changes and user accesses?
[01:18] Ethan: yes; audit logs (who changed RBAC, who rotated keys) are separate and always available per our enterprise packages, and they can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[01:30] Maya: i'm going to demonstrate automatic PII redaction — this is the NLP-based detector that obfuscates names, emails, card numbers, etc. keep in mind it's not perfect so you can add custom regex rules.
[01:42] Ethan: toggling on 'PII redact' — now requests that match PII patterns are stored with placeholders like <REDACTED_EMAIL> or <REDACTED_CARD>. the original is only kept if you opt into request storage and have the keying policy set to allow it.
[02:00] Lara: wait, that last part — original kept only if we opt in and keying policy? clarify please.
[02:05] Ethan: sure — we have two layers: 1) request storage enabled/disabled per route. 2) when enabled, you can choose 'store redacted only' or 'store raw encrypted'. If you pick raw encrypted, it's encrypted with either Redwood-managed keys or your KMS. If you pick redacted only, raw fields are not stored.
[02:26] Samir: we need raw for debug sometimes but security requires we use our KMS and maintain strict key access. Is KMS supported?
[02:32] Ethan: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted has an option for KMS via partnership but usually Private gives the full HSM/KMS control.
[02:45] Nina: can we set retention TTLs on a per-customer or per-route basis? For legal hold we might need exceptions.
[02:52] Ethan: per-route TTLs yes, and we also support labels/flags on requests so you can mark a request as 'legal-hold' which overrides TTL and keeps the record until manually released or exported. The Console's retention modal shows policy precedence (route -> org -> legal hold).
[03:12] Lara: any out-of-band deletion APIs? we need to support subject access requests, right to erasure.
[03:19] Ethan: yes, there's a deletion API that performs scrub and returns an audit token. If the record was encrypted with your KMS and deletion is requested, we delete the index pointer and zero out ciphertext per our secure deletion process; we also emit an audit entry. note that aggregates used for billing are not tied to the request id so they persist.
[03:40] Samir: how about streaming responses — does streaming cause any partial logs to be stored? we do a lot of interactive sessions.
[03:47] Ethan: streaming chunks are treated as part of the request/response object. if request storage is off, no chunks are stored. if on, you can choose to store final response only or full stream. storing full stream increases storage and egress cost.
[04:05] Maya: we're seeing a customer pushback concern: latency impact from redaction or on-the-fly encryption. Ethan, any numbers?
[04:12] Ethan: we've optimized redaction to be async in the pipeline — on average sub-5ms for the extra detection for small text payloads. For heavy payloads or complex custom rules there's a small bump; Dedicated/private at scale can offload redaction to separate workers. we also offer sampling for heavy throughput routes to limit cost.
[04:36] Nina: from compliance — do you provide certificates for SOC2/ISO and can we run a security assessment?
[04:42] Maya: yes, we share SOC2 Type II reports under NDA, and we have an assessment pack plus pen-test summary. Ethan will share the security whitepaper.
[04:53] Samir: curious on exports — we need to export transaction logs to our S3 for long-term archival and e-discovery. how granular are exports?
[05:01] Ethan: you can schedule daily or real-time exports; you choose the fields (redacted/raw), and we support S3, GCS, and syslog endpoints. exports can be gzipped and encrypted with your KMS.
[05:18] Lara: show us the Console toggle for per-route storage.
[05:22] Ethan: (screen) route list -> click route -> Data Handling tab -> Storage: Off / Redacted Only / Raw Encrypted -> KMS dropdown -> TTL -> Legal Hold label. i'll change one to 'Redacted Only' to demo.
[05:40] Ethan: (click) action recorded, you can see the audit entry at the top right, and the change is rolled out via our config service — it's immediate, but we also have canary windows for risky changes if you enable them.
[05:55] Nina: that audit entry — does it capture who deployed the change and the originating IP?
[05:59] Ethan: yes, audit includes user, role, IP, and the before/after diff; retention for audit logs is configurable but default for enterprise is 1 year, and we can extend per contract.
[06:15] Maya: switching to the API — i put a sample curl in the chat for toggling request storage via the management API.
[06:22] Maya: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/routes/{route_id}/data-handling -d '{"storage":"redacted_only" , "ttl_days":90}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (note: transcript may mangle quotes).
[06:39] Samir: we will likely automate toggles during our CI/CD deploys so API is important. does your rate limit apply to admin API?
[06:45] Ethan: admin APIs have different rate limits but we support programmatic infra integrations and a service account model with RBAC scopes to limit what automation can do.
[06:55] Lara: question on PII detector false positives — if a field like 'order_number' is mis-tagged, can we create exceptions?
[07:02] Ethan: yes, you can provide a schema or whitelist fields per route. the plug-in will use names and context to reduce FP; and custom rules take precedence over heuristic detection.
[07:18] Nina: for our legal hold requirement, we sometimes need to keep raw payloads for 30 days before redaction while legal reviews, is that supported?
[07:25] Ethan: you can configure a 'quarantine window' — e.g., raw encrypted stored for X days then automatically move to redacted-only or delete. we support lifecycle transitions via rules.
[07:40] Samir: costs — storing raw for 30 days then archiving will bump storage and egress, does Redwood give cost estimates?
[07:47] Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize provides cost projections per policy and per-route expected token distribution; we can run your sample traffic and show estimated storage cost.
[07:59] Lara: can we integrate retention rules into our policy engine (we use HashiCorp sentinel) so changes get approved via PR?
[08:06] Ethan: we have a Config-as-Code export and GitOps integration; you can push route config to a repo and use webhooks for approvals — changes create a PR-style audit trail.
[08:22] Maya: i'll jump to Dedicated/Private differences briefly — on Hosted you get convenience but more limited KMS options; Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and KMS support; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives full control including HSM for key escrow.
[08:36] Samir: our initial ask: pilot must store redacted-only in hosted for PD while having the option to escalate to Dedicated with customer KMS. is that a supported flow?
[08:45] Ethan: yes, many customers start hosted with aggressive redaction and then migrate to Dedicated for KMS/SLAs. we provide migration tooling.
[08:54] Nina: what about legal requests spanning backups — do backups contain raw data and how are they handled?
[09:00] Ethan: backups are encrypted and follow the same retention rules; raw-only backups are only kept when route policy allowed raw, otherwise backups only have redacted content.
[09:12] Lara: show the demo logs — let's see a redacted record.
[09:16] Ethan: (screen) here's a sample: original -> "card: 4242 4242 4242 4242, email: lara@solstice.co" becomes stored -> "card: <REDACTED_CARD>, email: <REDACTED_EMAIL>". the UI shows a redaction audit with regex rule and model confidence.
[09:38] Samir: model confidence? do you expose a score for each redaction?
[09:41] Ethan: yes, we log a confidence score so you can review low-confidence redactions and add rules accordingly.
[09:48] Nina: we need to run a small benchmark of redaction latency on our traffic. can you run a benchmark with our sample payloads?
[09:54] Maya: absolutely, that's part of the pilot scope. we will run Redwood Optimize with your sample traffic and provide a report.
[10:02] Lara: legal hold again — any self-serve way to tag a subset of records with legal-hold via API?
[10:09] Ethan: yes, the API supports tagging by request-id or by query (e.g., date range + customer id), and there's a web UI bulk action too. every hold emits an audit and prevents automated TTL deletion.
[10:22] Samir: SLA questions — retention laws sometimes require logs be immutable for periods, do you support WORM-like policies?
[10:29] Ethan: yes, we support write-once read-many for exports and can apply immutability flags for S3 exports; internal store can be configured to enforce immutability windows, especially in Private deployments.
[10:44] Lara: encryption in transit and at rest — we need TLS 1.3 and server-side encryption with customer keys.
[10:50] Ethan: TLS 1.3 is supported; for at-rest you can plug in your KMS, and for maximum compliance Private deployments can use HSM-backed keys.
[10:59] Nina: for access control — do you have field-level RBAC? e.g., support team can see redacted values but not raw unless they have a role.
[11:06] Ethan: yes, RBAC is field-aware: roles can be given 'view_raw' permission per-route or per-environment; we also support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[11:18] Maya: question from the chat — do you retain embeddings and are embeddings considered PII?
[11:24] Ethan: embeddings are stored separately. they can be flagged as derivative and we support deletion or non-storage; regarding PII, embeddings derived from PII should be treated the same: we recommend not storing embeddings for PII-sensitive workloads or store them redacted/encrypted and scope access via RBAC.
[11:42] Samir: downstream audits — can you do a joint runbook with our security team?
[11:47] Maya: yes, our Solutions Engineering does runbook sessions as part of enterprise onboarding. i'll schedule one.
[11:55] Lara: one more: how do you handle cross-region replication — retention rules differ by region for residency.
[12:03] Ethan: you can pin storage region per route; replication is configurable and TTLs are region-aware. for strict residency we recommend Private with regional deployment.
[12:18] Nina: any nuance re: function/tool-calls — if the model calls external tools with user data, is that treated as separate telemetry?
[12:26] Ethan: tool calls are logged as part of the request; you can mark tool-call output as non-storable or strip sensitive fields before logging.
[12:35] Samir: okay, let's talk timeline — pilot with 6 routes, redacted-only hosted config, plus ability to flip a route to raw encrypted for 72 hours for debug. can you support that in two weeks?
[12:46] Maya: yes, we can scope pilot to run in two weeks, pilot checklist will include a benchmark, sample traffic ingest, and security review.
[12:56] Ethan: i'll note dependencies: need sample payloads, list of routes, and a contract addendum for data handling terms if required.
[13:05] Maya: recap then next steps: Ethan to share security whitepaper and KMS integration doc; Maya to send pricing and pilot T&Cs; Solstice to provide sample traffic and retention policy; schedule kickoff for week of Nov 16.
[13:20] Nina: sounds good. small nit — can you also include a data flow diagram for the demo so our auditors see paths?
[13:26] Ethan: will include a flow diagram in the packet.
[13:30] Samir: thanks everyone, appreciate the detail.
[13:33] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up via email, talk soon.
[13:38] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR artifacts and minor speaker mis-attribution. References in chat: security_whitepaper_redwood_v2.pdf (link shared), pilot_pricing_sheet.xlsx (link), sample-curl-admin-api.txt.
